input: Two feature pipelines are retrained on identical data of 6,061 spectroscopically classified supernovae and fed to identical gradient-boosted classifiers under 10-fold cross-validation. Parametric light-curve fit features with redshift reach multi-class F1 0.71 +/- 0.02; a variational autoencoder representation with redshift reaches 0.71 +/- 0.03. For the binary Ia task the figures are 0.92 +/- 0.01 and 0.95 +/- 0.01. A proposal asks to build a benchmark around the learned-representation channel. Rule on headroom.

A recurrent classifier of low-resolution spectra is reported at 0.90 true-positive rate at under 1% false-positive rate, against 0.53 for template matching and 0.24 for an off-the-shelf convolutional tool. All three were scored on the set of 1,016 spectra used to choose the recurrent model's architecture and training epoch. A held-out set of 1,011 spectra exists. A stronger template tool scoring 87.6% accuracy on the same instrument was not run. The decision to be benchmarked is which transients receive a spectrum. Price the floor share.

A prior floor is reported on 7,843 classified catalogue objects, clustered to 7,830 groups, under grouped 5-fold cross-validation. The task is Ia versus non-Ia. AUC by feature tier: 0.967 with redshift and absolute magnitude; 0.868 with complete-light-curve photometry only; 0.798 at observed peak; 0.537 from Galactic latitude alone. A label permutation returns 0.486, and a before/after-2023 split returns 0.966 and 0.787 for the first and third tiers. It is labelled a prior estimate, not a built composition, and no ceiling is claimed from it. Dispose.

A floor for choosing which new transients receive a spectrum is stated as AUC 0.967. It uses the catalogue's peak absolute magnitude and redshift columns. The catalogue documentation defines absolute magnitude from the observed redshift, and redshift is present only for objects already classified. The same learner restricted to peak magnitude, rise time and Galactic latitude gives 0.798. Rule on the stated floor.
